opening.text: Think of a long road trip with someone you love. There are good miles and boring miles. There's a flat tire somewhere. There are songs and silence. But the best part isn't the place you reach. It's who is in the seat beside you. A marriage that lasts forever is like that road trip.

mainMessage.text: Eternal marriage isn't a finish line. It's a journey we take together, with God in the car.

blocks.text: **The road begins with a promise** From the start, God said it was not good for us to be alone. He gave us each other to travel with.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
The trip is longer than this life.
**God joins the two** The Savior taught that God Himself joins a husband and wife. In the temple, that bond is sealed.

And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
The sacred ordinance binds us together with our eternal companion and with God.
Three are in this marriage: husband, wife and God.
**Each needs the other** Paul said that in the Lord, neither is complete without the other. Each brings something the other lacks.
Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
To be together with the spouse you love forever truly sounds like heaven.
Together is better.
**Kindness on the long road** On a long trip, small kindnesses matter most. Paul said to be kind, tender and ready to forgive.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Love the Savior, and love for each other grows.
**The highest place** The Lord teaches that the highest degree of glory requires the new and everlasting covenant of marriage.

In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood \[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage\];
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
Celestial marriage is a pivotal part of preparation for eternal life.
This road leads somewhere wonderful.
**Two, with the Lord, are strong** Solomon wrote that two are better than one. A cord of three strands is hard to break.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
We believe in eternal marriage, we teach of eternal marriage, and we seek an eternal marriage.
Seek it, and keep seeking it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when love in marriage was shown by patience or sacrifice. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jacob works for Rachel

blocks.text: Jacob loved Rachel. He worked seven years to marry her.
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
Love makes long waiting feel short. Eternal love is worth the patience.

application.text: First, think of one thing your spouse does that helps you. Second, thank them for it today. Third, plan a small time together this week with no phones.

opening.text: A rowboat has two oars. If one person rows and the other doesn't, the boat goes in circles. But when both pull together, it glides. A good marriage is like that boat. Two people, each with an oar, working toward the same shore.

mainMessage.text: Eternal marriage works when both partners row together, with the Lord as the one who sets the course.

blocks.text: **The boat was made for two** God made us for company. He said it is not good to be alone.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
The voyage goes on forever.
**The Lord launches the boat** God joins a husband and wife. In the temple, He seals them together for time and for eternity.

And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
The sacred ordinance binds us together with our eternal companion and with God.
He launched it, and He is in it.
**One oar isn't enough** A boat with one oar spins. Husband and wife each bring what the other needs.
Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
To be together with the spouse you love forever truly sounds like heaven.
Two oars make the boat go straight.
**Smooth water takes kindness** When the water is rough, kind words keep a boat steady. Paul said to be kind and forgiving.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Love for the Savior steadies the boat.
**The far shore** The shore ahead is the celestial kingdom. The Lord says the highest degree needs the new and everlasting covenant.

In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood \[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage\];
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
Celestial marriage is a pivotal part of preparation for eternal life.
Keep rowing toward the far shore.
**A third strand in the rope** The boat is tied to the dock by a cord of three strands. With God as the third, it is hard to break.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
We believe in eternal marriage, we teach of eternal marriage, and we seek an eternal marriage.
With God, the cord holds.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they and their spouse worked together to get through something hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Isaac and Rebekah

blocks.text: Rebekah left her family to marry a man she had never met. Isaac welcomed her.
And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
Their marriage began with trust, and Isaac found comfort in his wife. Marriage can be a place of comfort for both.

application.text: First, ask your spouse what would help them most this week. Second, do that one thing. Third, share how you felt after.

opening.text: A great bridge stands on two towers. Neither tower carries it alone. Each one holds up its side, and the cables between them share the weight. If one tower is weak, the whole bridge is at risk. A marriage is a lot like that. Two people, each standing firm, with a strong bond between them.

mainMessage.text: Eternal marriage is a bridge built on two towers and strengthened by God. Both must stand, and both must stay connected.

blocks.text: **The bridge was planned** From the beginning, God planned for two people to share life's load. He said it is not good to be alone.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
A bridge is made for the long crossing.

And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.

Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

To be together with the spouse you love forever truly sounds like heaven.
Both towers matter.
**Maintenance, not neglect** Bridges need regular care. So do marriages. Small repairs, kindness and forgiveness keep the bridge sound.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Mend small cracks early.
**Where the bridge leads** The bridge leads to the highest glory. The Lord says it requires the new and everlasting covenant of marriage.

In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood \[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage\];
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
Celestial marriage is a pivotal part of preparation for eternal life.
The bridge ends in glory.
**A cable of three strands** The cables that hold a bridge are braided from many strands. With God as the third strand, the marriage is hard to break.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
We believe in eternal marriage, we teach of eternal marriage, and we seek an eternal marriage.
Build it to last.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they and their spouse stood together through a hard time. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Adam and Eve rejoice together

blocks.text: Adam and Eve faced a hard world together. They also found joy together.

And in that day Adam blessed God and was filled, and began to prophesy concerning all the families of the earth, saying: Blessed be the name of God, for because of my transgression my eyes are opened, and in this life I shall have joy, and again in the flesh I shall see God. And Eve, his wife, heard all these things and was glad, saying: Were it not for our transgression we never should have had seed, and never should have known good and evil, and the joy of our redemption, and the eternal life which God giveth unto all the obedient.
They stood side by side and looked ahead with hope. A strong marriage does the same.

application.text: First, think of a weak spot in your relationship. Second, pick one kind act that would strengthen it. Third, do that act this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God designed marriage to be strong. I know He holds it together when we turn to Him. I know Jesus Christ is the foundation. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A good garden doesn't happen by accident. Someone waters it. Someone pulls weeds. Someone shows up every day, even when it's hot. After a while, things start to bloom. A marriage is like that garden. It needs daily care. When it gets it, it grows beautifully.

mainMessage.text: Eternal marriage grows with daily care. Small, steady acts of love are the water and sun.

blocks.text: **The garden was God's idea** In the beginning, God planted a garden and put two people in it. He said they shouldn't be alone.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
Gardens grow over seasons.
**Planted by God** A garden planted by God has deep roots. In the temple, God Himself joins a husband and wife.

And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
The sacred ordinance binds us together with our eternal companion and with God.
The roots go deep.
**Two kinds of care** One gardener may water and the other may weed. Each does what the other can't. Neither is whole without the other.
Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
To be together with the spouse you love forever truly sounds like heaven.
Together, the garden thrives.
**Pull the weeds of hurt** Resentment grows like a weed if no one pulls it. Kindness and forgiveness keep the garden clear.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Forgive quickly, and the garden stays healthy.
**The harvest** The fruit of this garden is eternal. The Lord says the highest glory requires the new and everlasting covenant of marriage.

In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood \[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage\];
Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy said this in his talk “Fruit That Remains” from the April 2024 general conference.
Celestial marriage is a pivotal part of preparation for eternal life.
The harvest is worth the work.
**Weather the storms together** Storms come to every garden. Two people, held by a third strand, can bear them.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference.

Keep tending it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when working side by side with a spouse brought them closer. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Aquila and Priscilla

blocks.text: Aquila and Priscilla were a married couple who worked at the same trade. Paul stayed with them and worked beside them.

And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them. And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
They are always named together. They worked, served and taught as a team. That is what a garden tended by two looks like.

application.text: First, pick one daily habit for your marriage, like a kind word each morning. Second, do it for seven days. Third, notice what grows.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that marriage grows with care. I know God blesses those who tend it. I know Jesus Christ is the Master Gardener. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

When a storm hits, they hold each other up. A marriage that lasts is like that. Two lives, growing together, rooted in the same soil.

Growth takes a lifetime and more.

In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood \[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage\];

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to stand by their spouse in a storm. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph takes Mary as his wife

blocks.text: Joseph had many reasons to be afraid. An angel spoke to him in a dream. He chose to stay.
Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:
He trusted God, and he stayed by her side. Faithful marriages are often built by choices like that one.

application.text: First, think of a storm your marriage has faced. Second, thank your spouse for standing by you in it. Third, ask what you can do now to help them feel held.
